items.text: Europe has faced an unusually early and intense heatwave, with Germany experiencing nearly 40°C and Spain reaching up to 43°C in cities like Seville. This extreme heat has caused wildfires in Spain, killing two farmers, and resulted in heat-related deaths in France, along with hundreds of hospitalizations. Iconic landmarks such as the Eiffel Tower closed temporarily due to the dangerous temperatures. Climate scientists warn that Europe is now the fastest-warming continent, warming twice as fast as the global average. Several factors combine to amplify this warming: melting Arctic ice reduces sunlight reflection, drying rivers and lakes cause the land to heat more, cleaner air increases sunshine, and the Mediterranean Sea is heating rapidly. These changes contribute to increasingly frequent and severe summer heatwaves. Experts emphasize the urgent need for both deep cuts in greenhouse gas emissions and upgrades to infrastructure, such as cooling centers, green urban spaces, and protections for vulnerable people. However, even nations with advanced systems are struggling to adapt to this accelerating climate crisis. Difficult words: iconic (very famous or popular), amplify (to make something larger or greater in amount, importance, etc.), upgrade (an increase in improvement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Europe is suffering a very strong heatwave. In Germany, temperatures reached nearly 40°C, and in Spain, they climbed to 43°C. The heat caused wildfires in Spain that killed two farmers. In France, two people died and hundreds ended up in the hospital because of heat illness. The Eiffel Tower had to close because it was too hot. Scientists say Europe is warming faster than anywhere else. This is because ice in the Arctic is melting , rivers and lakes are drying up, clean air lets in more sun, and the Mediterranean Sea is getting hotter. Experts warn that governments need to reduce pollution and build cooling centers and green areas. Even rich countries are finding it hard to cope with the rising heat. Difficult words: melt (to turn into water), pollution (bad substances in the air, water, or land), cope (to deal with a problem or difficult situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Europe is very hot now. In Germany, it is nearly 40°C. In Spain, it is 43°C. The heat is dangerous. Two farmers died in a fire in Spain. In France, people go to the hospital. They feel sick from the heat. Some places, such as the Eiffel Tower, must close because it is too hot. Scientists say that Europe is getting hotter faster than other places. Ice in the Arctic melts , rivers and lakes dry up, the sea gets warm, and the sun makes everything hotter. People need places to cool down and shade . Even rich countries have problems keeping people safe in this hot weather. Difficult words: heat (when it is hot outside), melt (to turn into water), shade (a cool place away from the sun). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A BBC investigation has shown that illegal tobacco sales are rising in mini marts across British high streets. Police and Trading Standards are struggling to stop the problem. Criminal gangs are said to be behind the trade, making profits equal to selling hard drugs like heroin. Some shops even employ asylum seekers with no right to work. Officials describe the situation as a war, but they say they don’t have enough resources. Police found hidden tunnels and stashes of illegal cigarettes under shop floors. Some people who work in these shops don’t take the issue seriously, even when they lose thousands of pounds. One man with a criminal record was angry when BBC reporters uncovered the secret storage areas. The problem is not limited to one city. In Hull, undercover teams found hundreds of shops selling smuggled cigarettes. These sales are linked to modern slavery, drug crime, and money laundering . Despite fines and arrests, some shops reopen and sell again the same day. Difficult words: mini mart (a small supermarket), stash (a secret supply of something), money laundering (illegally concealing the origin of money obtained from illegal activities). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A BBC report showed that many mini marts in the UK sell illegal cigarettes. Police and authorities say it is hard to stop this problem. They think gangs bring the cigarettes and make a lot of money. Some workers in these shops are asylum seekers who cannot work legally. Workers hide cigarettes in tunnels under shop floors. One shop had many bags full of smuggled cigarettes. Even when the police discover a shop, it sometimes opens again soon. In the city of Hull, reporters found many shops selling illegal tobacco. This crime is now usual on British high streets. Experts say this business is very big and can be like drug selling. It also brings other crimes, such as illegal business with people and money crimes. Difficult words: mini mart (a small supermarket), asylum seeker (a person who leaves their country to find a safe place to live), smuggle (to bring things into a country secretly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many shops in the UK sell bad cigarettes. These cigarettes are not legal . Police want to stop it, but it is difficult. Some people who work in the shops are not allowed to work in the UK. The cigarettes are under the floor in the shop. They are in bags and boxes. Some people laugh about it. Some shops open again after the police leave. Reporters go to many shops. They find illegal cigarettes in many places. Some shops sell other bad things too. This makes a big problem. Police and other workers try to help, but it is not easy. Police say this activity is as bad as selling hard drugs. Difficult words: legal (possible by law), allowed (when you can do something, or when something can happen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Liverpool footballer Diogo Jota died in a car crash in Spain, along with his brother André. Police said the car lost control after a tyre burst during an overtaking attempt. It crashed and caught fire. Jota was 28 and had just won the Premier League with Liverpool. He also got married in June and had three children. Jota played 182 games for Liverpool, scoring 65 goals. He also helped the team win the FA Cup and League Cup. He played for Portugal 49 times. His death shocked many people, both in Portugal and abroad, because he was still young and full of potential . People around the world, including Cristiano Ronaldo and Jürgen Klopp, shared their sadness online. Fans brought flowers to Anfield Stadium and flags were lowered to half-mast . Jota was praised not only for being a talented player but also for being a loving father and husband. A minute of silence will be held at UEFA Women’s Euro matches in his honour. Difficult words: potential (the possibility to grow or achieve something), half-mast (the position of a flag which is being flown some way below the top as a mark of respect for a person who has died). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Diogo Jota, a football player from Liverpool, died in a car crash in Spain. His brother André died too. Their car went off the road, and the police said the tyre broke when they tried to overtake another vehicle. The car caught fire. Jota was 28 years old. He won the Premier League and got married in June. Jota played 182 matches for Liverpool and scored 65 goals. He played for Portugal 49 times. People in Portugal and other countries said he had a great future, and his death shocked them. Many people felt very sad, and players like Cristiano Ronaldo and Jürgen Klopp said kind things about him online. Fans left flowers outside the stadium. Flags went down to half-mast . UEFA said there will be a minute of silence before games. Difficult words: overtake (to go past another car), shock (to upset or surprise someone suddenly), half-mast (when a flag is halfway down to show respect for someone who died). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Diogo Jota is a football player. He plays for Liverpool. Diogo and his brother are in a car. The car goes very fast. The tyre breaks. The car leaves the road and starts to burn. Diogo and his brother die. Diogo is 28. He has a wife and three children. Diogo plays many games. He scores many goals. He helps his team win. He plays for Portugal. Many people love him. They say that he is a great player and a great dad. Many people feel sad. His friends talk about him. Fans go to the stadium . They bring flowers. The club puts the flag down. This shows respect. People in Portugal also feel sad. Difficult words: tyre (a rubber ring on a car’s wheel), stadium (a place where people watch sports), flag (a piece of cloth with colors or a country or team). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two European brown bears, Mish and Lucy, escaped from their enclosure at Wildwood Devon, a wildlife park near Ottery St Mary, UK. The five-year-old bears used the opportunity to eat a week’s supply of honey from the park’s food storage. The park stated that no visitors were ever in danger; however, as a safety measure , all guests were quickly moved to a secure building. Park staff monitored the bears using CCTV and kept a close watch on the ground. Eventually, Mish returned to the enclosure by himself, while Lucy was tempted back using a bell and her favorite treats. The bears then fell asleep peacefully. Police were called to the scene as a standard safety measure, and an investigation is ongoing to understand how the escape happened. Mish and Lucy were originally rescued from a snow drift in Albania in 2019. Wildwood Devon confirmed the bear exhibit is now secure and praised staff and visitors for their calm cooperation. Difficult words: enclosure (a closed area where animals are kept), measure (a plan or course of action taken to achieve a particular purpose), tempted (wanting to have or do something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Two brown bears escaped from their cage at Wildwood Devon in the UK. The bears, Mish and Lucy, are five years old. After escaping, they found the food store and ate a week’s worth of honey. The park said no people were in danger. Visitors stayed in a safe building. Park staff watched the bears using cameras and followed them on the ground. Mish went back to his cage on his own. Lucy came back when the workers rang a bell and gave her her favorite food. Both bears then fell asleep. Police came to the park as part of safety rules . The park says the cage is now safe. Now, the park is checking how the bears got out. Mish and Lucy were saved in Albania in 2019. Difficult words: escape (to get out from a place), cage (a space with bars to keep animals in), safety rules (things to do to stay safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two big bears get out from their cage at Wildwood Devon, a park in the UK. The bears’ names are Mish and Lucy. They are five years old. They find food and eat lots of honey. People at the park go to a safe room. The park says that no one is in danger . Workers watch the bears with cameras. Mish goes back by himself. Lucy goes back when she hears a bell and gets her best food. After that, they both go to sleep. Police come to help. The park is looking at how the bears get out. The bears are OK now. They come from Albania in 2019. Now, the cage is safe again. Difficult words: cage (a space with bars where animals stay), safe (when nothing bad can happen to you), danger (the situation when something bad can happen to you). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Maryinka, a town in Ukraine’s Donetsk region destroyed by war, Galina Nevinnaya lives alone. She was the last person to leave during the Russian shelling in 2022, which gave her a concussion and trapped her in a basement. Rescued by soldiers, she became the first and only person to return nearly three years later. Before the war, around 10,000 people lived in Maryinka. Now, it is almost empty. Her mother was killed in April 2022. Galina spends her days repairing her ruined house. She says some damage was caused by NATO weapons, though this couldn’t be confirmed. She survives using water from a well and finding food however she can. When asked why she came back, she answered with a proverb: ‘He who lives in his own home lives well.’ In 2023, President Putin declared the town under Russian control, although most countries don’t accept Russia’s claim to the region. Galina’s story shows the deep cost of war and strong personal resilience . Difficult words: concussion (a brain injury from a hit or explosion), well (a deep hole to get water from the ground), resilience (the strength to recover or keep going after hard times). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Galina Nevinnaya lives alone in Maryinka, a destroyed town in Ukraine. She left during the fighting in 2022 after getting hurt and trapped in a basement. Soldiers helped her escape. Now, almost three years later, she is the only person to return. Her town once had 10,000 people, but most are away now. Her mother died in the war in April 2022. Galina is fixing her house, which was badly damaged. She says NATO rockets caused some of it, but this is not proven . She gets water from a well and finds food by herself. When a reporter asked her why she returned, she said, ‘He who lives in his own home lives well.’ In 2023, Russia said Maryinka was under its control, but many countries don’t agree. Galina’s life shows how hard the war is. Difficult words: trapped (unable to move or escape from a place or situation), proven (tested or shown to be true), well (a deep hole for water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Galina Nevinnaya lives alone in Maryinka, a town in Ukraine. The town is in a war in 2022. Galina leaves in 2022 after bombs hurt her. She is in a basement . She cannot move. Soldiers save her. Now, Galina is back. She is the only person there. Before, 10,000 people live in the town. Now. It is empty. Galina’s mother dies in 2022. Galina works on her house. She must repair it. She gets water from a well . She finds food herself. People ask why she comes back. She says, ‘He who lives in his own home lives well.’ In 2023, Russia says it controls the town. Many countries say that this is not okay. Difficult words: basement (the room under a house), repair (to make something work or okay again), well (a deep hole for water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Tens of thousands of people gathered in Budapest to mark the 30th anniversary of Pride despite an official ban from the Hungarian government. Many attendees, including European politicians and first-time marchers, joined to support LGBTQ+ rights and civil liberties . Greta Thunberg also took part and strongly criticized Prime Minister Viktor Orbán’s policies, calling the ban a threat to human rights. Although Pride was banned, far-right groups were allowed to march with police permission. This double standard caused criticism. Opposition leader Péter Magyar didn’t attend, stating he was on holiday with his sons. However, he posted a supportive message online, calling for unity and the protection of all Hungarians. Analysts believe Orbán used the ban to pressure Magyar to speak about liberal topics, possibly to divide his voter base . Still, Pride became a symbol of resistance . Even with tight police control and threats from the government, the march ended without major incidents. Participants showed courage and called for freedom and equality. Difficult words: civil liberty (a basic right to be free and treated equally), voter base (the core group of supporters who always vote for a political party), resistance (fighting against control or unfair treatment). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many people joined the 30th Budapest Pride march, even though the Hungarian government banned it. People wanted to support LGBTQ+ rights and freedom. Some European politicians and Greta Thunberg joined, too. She said the ban was an attack on human rights. At the same time, far-right groups were allowed to march. This made many people angry. The police kept both groups safe and away from each other. The leader of the opposition party, Péter Magyar, didn’t come. He said he was on holiday with his sons. Still, he shared a message to support the march. Experts think the government wanted to make him talk about difficult topics like LGBTQ+ rights. But he spoke more about daily problems in Hungary, such as high prices, poor health care, and bad roads. Difficult words: allowed (when somebody lets you do or have something), opposition (a big political party which is not in a government), topic (a thing to talk about). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many people go to the Budapest Pride. The government bans the march , but the people come anyway. They want to help LGBTQ+ people. Some people come for the first time. Greta Thunberg comes, too. She says that the ban is not good. Some other people make a far-right march. The police say yes to them. The police keep the groups apart. It is safe. Péter Magyar, the leader of the opposition party, is not there. He is with his sons. He writes a nice message to all people. Magyar talks about money, hospitals, and schools. The government wants him to talk about Pride. He does not. Pride ends with no big problems. People are happy and strong. Difficult words: ban (a rule which stops something), march (when many people walk along roads as a form of protest), far-right (people with strong political ideas), opposition (a big political party which is not in a government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of small boats are preparing for the new fishing season in Nouadhibou, Mauritania. Local and foreign fishermen depend on this work to feed their families. They often face harsh and dangerous conditions. Fish like sardinella are essential for food and jobs in the region. However, fishermen now need to go further out to sea, as these fish are harder to find. Scientists report that many species are overfished and need urgent protection. Industrial ships and fish meal factories have increased fishing pressure. Some companies say they follow sustainable practices, but not all do. Without enough fish, even large factories stop production. A strong management plan is needed to control when, where, and how fish are caught. The plan includes cooperation between Mauritania and the European Union. The EU supports Mauritania by helping improve ports, fish markets, and research centers. The goal is to make sure fishing provides food, jobs, and income without damaging fish populations in the long term. Difficult words: overfished (when people catch too many fish, so the number becomes too low), sustainable (able to continue without causing harm). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many small boats get ready to fish near Nouadhibou in Mauritania. Fishermen from different countries need this work to live. Fish like sardinella give food and jobs to many people. But it is harder to catch fish now, and fishermen must go far out to sea. Scientists say some fish are in danger because people catch too many. Big ships and fish meal factories also catch a lot of fish. Some factories try to protect fish, but others don’t. Sometimes, there are no fish for days. People want better rules for fishing, which would help fish stay in the sea. Mauritania and the European Union work together. The EU gives money to build better fish markets and ports . This helps people sell fish and protect fish for the future. Difficult words: protect (to keep safe), port (a town or city near water where ships come). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many boats go to the sea near Nouadhibou in Mauritania. Fishermen from different countries want to catch fish. Fish give food and money. But it is not an easy job. The men stay on the sea for many days. Some fish are not easy to find now. People catch too many fish. Big ships and factories take fish for other things, too. Some factories try to help the sea, but some do not. Mauritania and Europe work together. The EU gives money to build better fish markets . They build better places for boats. They want people to eat fish and have money. But they also want the sea to stay full of fish. Difficult words: fisherman (a person who catches fish), market (a place to buy and sell things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Croatia used to be known as a low-cost holiday spot on the Adriatic, but in recent years, it has become more expensive. Gracia Horvatin, who has worked in tourism for decades, runs a restaurant that grew from a small family tavern . Like the tourism industry in Croatia, her business has developed and adapted to changes. Today, high inflation, labor shortages , and state costs have caused prices to increase. However, many businesses, like Gracia’s, choose not to raise prices again. Tourist behavior is also changing. Visitors, especially from Germany and Austria, now prefer shorter stays and want to explore more places. Long-time guests notice that prices are higher, especially since the Euro was introduced, but they also admit that the quality of services has improved. The Croatian tourist board argues that the country still offers good value. However, there is concern that rising prices may keep locals away from their coast in the future. Difficult words: tavern (a small restaurant or bar), labor shortage (not enough workers for the jobs). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Croatia was a cheap place for holidays, but now it is more expensive. Gracia Horvatin started with a small tavern and now has a restaurant. She doesn’t want to raise prices, even if food costs more. Prices are going up because of inflation and not enough workers. Many tourists now visit more places in a short time instead of staying in one place. Most guests are from Germany, Austria, and Slovenia. Some people say prices are high, but they also say service is better now. The tourist office says Croatia still gives good value . But locals worry that one day they will not be able to enjoy the coast. Prices are going up, but the biggest problem is how to give good service and quality. Difficult words: tavern (a small restaurant), inflation (when things cost more than before), value (how good something is for the price). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Croatia is not cheap now. It is more expensive than before. A lady named Gracia has a small place. She gives food to people. She does not want to make meals cost more. But it is hard to find workers. People do not stay long in one place anymore. They go to many places. Most people come from Germany, Austria, and Slovenia. Some people say that prices are high. But they also say that things are better now. The tourist group says Croatia is still good. But people in Croatia are not happy. They may not have money to go to the beach. The most important thing is to help people and give good service . Difficult words: expensive (when something costs a lot of money), service (the help of work that people give to tourists in hotels, restaurants, or shops). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez are hosting a high-profile wedding celebration in Venice, Italy. Originally planned in the busy nightlife district of Cannaregio, the party location was moved to the historic Arsenal area due to security concerns and fears of protests. The Arsenal, a 14th-century complex surrounded by water, becomes inaccessible by land when its bridges are raised. Around 200 to 250 VIP guests, including Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner, are expected to attend. The celebrations will last three days and are estimated to cost between 46 and 55 million dollars. The first private jets began arriving on Tuesday, and five luxury hotels in Venice have been fully booked. Organizers also arranged at least 30 water taxis for transporting guests. Local activists, including the No Space for Bezos group, criticized the event, saying it turns Venice into a playground for the wealthy. However, they called the move to the isolated Arsenal a great victory. The exact date and location of the wedding ceremony remain confidential . Difficult words: inaccessible (a place that is difficult to get to), confidential (kept secret or private). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez will have a big wedding party in Venice, Italy. At first, the party was planned in a busy area called Cannaregio. But now, it will happen in a quiet, old place called the Arsenal. This place is hard to reach because it is surrounded by water. Around 200 to 250 special guests will come. Some guests, like Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner, already arrived. The party will last three days and cost up to 55 million dollars. People are flying in with private jets, and five luxury hotels are fully booked. Some local people are not happy and plan peaceful protests. They say Venice is becoming a fun park for rich people. The exact day and place of the wedding are still a secret . Difficult words: surrounded (all around), luxury (expensive), secrets (something the others don’t know about). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez will get married in Venice. They first want to have a party in a busy area, but move it to a quiet place because of safety and protests. The new place is called the Arsenal. There is water around it. It is hard to get there when bridges are up. About 200 – 250 guests will come. The wedding is secret , but the party will be on Saturday. The event may cost around 46 – 55 million dollars. Bezos will give money to help Venice. Many guests are arriving in private jets. Some famous people, like Ivanka Trump, are already in Venice. Some people are not happy. They say that Venice is a fun park for rich people. Difficult words: safety (when you are safe), secret (something that others do not know about), guest (people who come to a party or event). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The murder of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in 2024 drew attention to “ghost guns” – untraceable firearms that can be made at home using 3D printers and shared blueprints . The suspect was found with one such weapon, partly made of plastic but able to fire multiple shots. These weapons have become more advanced and easier to build, despite being illegal in many places. Online platforms, such as Telegram and social media, play a key role in spreading information about 3D guns. Some users offer to sell and even ship these weapons internationally, violating laws. A BBC journalist contacted one seller, who casually admitted to his activity. While not all offers are real, scammers and actual dealers both use these channels. Although building a fully working 3D-printed gun is not simple, detailed guides and stronger materials have made it possible. Experts worry about the global spread, especially in areas with strict gun laws where these weapons may become the tool of choice of criminals, militia , or extremists. Authorities are struggling to respond with new laws and controls. Difficult words: blueprint (a design plan or technical drawing), untraceable (something that cannot be tracked or identified), militia (a group of people trained for military service, not part of the official army). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The murder of the United Healthcare CEO in 2024 helped people see the danger of 3D-printed ghost guns . People make these guns at home with a 3D printer, which makes them hard to trace. The police found one in the bag of the murder suspect. It could fire many bullets and was not easy to break. Many people learn how to make these guns online. On Telegram and other social media, people offer guns or parts and sometimes send them to other countries. A BBC reporter talked to one man selling these guns, who admitted it was illegal. Building these guns is not always easy, but more people are learning. Stronger tools and free guides help. Some places have strict gun laws, but 3D printing makes it harder to stop people. Authorities are now trying to catch up , but it is very difficult. Difficult words: ghost gun (a gun which you can make at home and nobody knows about it), admit (to say that something is true, especially something bad), catch up (to reach the same level or quality as someone or something else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A US health CEO dies in 2024. Somebody kills him with a gun. Police find the gun in the bag of the person they catch. The gun is from a 3D printer. It can shoot many times. Some people show how to make these guns online. They use Telegram and other apps. One man says he can send a gun to the UK. A BBC reporter calls him. The man says it is his job to sell guns. He knows that it is illegal . These guns are not easy to make, but many people try. They use metal and plastic. They follow simple steps from the internet. Some countries try to stop this. They want to make new laws . But criminals are ahead of the police. Difficult words: CEO (the top boss of a company or organization), illegal (against the official rules), law (a rule which the government makes). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Music festivals like Coachella, Burning Man, and Lollapalooza used to be exciting events for fans. People would travel far to see many bands, often discovering new ones. But now, rising ticket and travel costs are making many people choose not to go. Festivals can cost several hundred dollars or even up to 1000 dollars for a full experience, including transportation and lodging . Some fans now prefer to spend that money on other things, like travel abroad or online experiences. Last year, Burning Man didn’t sell out for the first time, and even Coachella had slower ticket sales. In 2024, over 1,100 festivals took place in the US, but around 40 were canceled. Experts say the way young people enjoy music is changing. Many prefer to stream concerts or join virtual festivals on gaming platforms like Fortnite and Roblox. Until prices fall or festivals offer something new, fewer people may attend live events. Difficult words: lodging (a place to sleep while traveling), stream (to watch or listen to something online). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Music festivals like Coachella and Burning Man were very popular in the past. People went to see famous bands and enjoy live music. But now, tickets and travel are too expensive for many people. Some say it costs too much to fly and stay at a festival. In 2024, there were over 1,000 music festivals in the US, but organizers canceled 40 of them. Even Coachella had fewer people. Fans don’t want to spend 600 dollars or more just to see a few bands. Young people also enjoy music in new ways. They stream concerts or watch them in games like Fortnite. Festivals must change or become cheaper, or fans may not return. Difficult words: festival (a big event with music or shows), cancel (to stop something what you planned), stream (to watch or listen to something online). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many people go to music festivals in the past. They want to see bands and have fun . Now, tickets and trips cost too much. Young people like to spend money on other things than expensive festivals. Some festivals in the US do not take place last year. Even big ones have fewer people. Some fans do not want to pay a lot to see just a few bands. Young people enjoy music in new ways. They use phones or games to watch shows. Festivals may need to change or be cheaper. Difficult words: have fun (to enjoy yourself or feel happy while doing something), ticket (paper or card to go into a show or place), fan (a person who likes something or someone a lot, like a singer, band, or sports team). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In northern Italy, Dr. Massimo Vacchetta has opened the country’s first clinic for hedgehogs. Located in a 300-year-old house in the commune of Novello, the clinic currently cares for around 200 injured or sick hedgehogs. Many suffer from dehydration , broken bones, or infections. Some patients are too weak to survive in the wild again, while others will be released once they recover. Hedgehogs are very important for nature. They control pests , and their presence shows that the environment is healthy. Sadly, their numbers are falling. They are on the red list of endangered animals because they are killed by cars, gardening tools, or fires. Pesticides and parasites also cause harm. Dr. Vacchetta and his team try to save every hedgehog, even if it means operating or treating life-threatening conditions. Though hedgehogs may seem strong, they are quite fragile . Many people across Italy now support the clinic, showing that small animals can have a big impact on nature. Difficult words: dehydration (when the body doesn’t have enough water), pest (an insect or other animal that attacks crops, food, or livestock), fragile (easily hurt or damaged). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Dr. Massimo Vacchetta has a clinic for hedgehogs in northern Italy. It is the first one in the country. He helps sick and hurt hedgehogs. Some of them are very weak , others can get better and go back to the wild. Now, the clinic has about 200 animals. Hedgehogs are good for nature. They eat bugs and help the environment . But many of them are in danger. Cars, fire, and garden tools hurt them. They also get sick from bugs or bad food. Dr. Vacchetta works every day to save them. He gives them food, medicine, and love. Many people help his clinic by sending money. These small animals are important to the world. Difficult words: clinic (a place where sick people or animals get help), weak (not strong), environment (the natural world around us). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A man in Italy helps small animals. His name is Dr. Massimo Vacchetta. He has a clinic for sick hedgehogs . Some are hurt. Some are sick. He gives them food and helps them get strong. Hedgehogs live in nature. They eat bugs. They help the Earth. But many hedgehogs die. Cars, fires, and garden tools hurt them. They also get sick from bugs or bad food. The doctor works every day. He gives water and care. Some hedgehogs get better. Some do not. People send money to help. These little animals are important. Difficult words: clinic (a place where sick people or animals get help), hedgehog (a small animal with sharp spikes), bug (a small insect). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Israel and the US carried out precise and powerful strikes on three major Iranian nuclear sites: Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan. The US used B-2 bombers with bunker-busting bombs to destroy deep underground facilities. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu praised the action, saying it may change history, and stressed the importance of peace through strength. Iran responded by firing 30 missiles at Israel, some of which hit cities in the north and central areas. Israeli air defenses worked to intercept them, but 16 people were injured. Most missiles were stopped, though sirens failed in one place. A think tank expert called the strike illegal under international law and warned it could backfire. He noted that Iran might withdraw from its nuclear treaty and continue enriching uranium secretly. He compared this to how Iraq expanded its nuclear efforts after an Israeli strike in 1981. He suggested diplomacy would have been a better and safer option. Difficult words: bunker-busting (destroying underground structures), intercept (to stop something before it reaches its target), think tank (a body of experts providing advice and ideas on specific political or economic problems). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The US and Israel attacked three nuclear sites in Iran: Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan. They used special bombs and planes to destroy the underground parts. The Israeli leader said this attack shows power and hopes it brings peace . Iran fired 30 missiles at Israel in return. Israel stopped many of them, but 16 people still got hurt because sirens didn’t work in one area. An expert said the attack is not okay by international rules. He said it could make Iran leave a big nuclear agreement and work secretly on its nuclear program. He compared it with what happened in Iraq in 1981. He thinks talking would be better than fighting. Difficult words: peace (the time without a war or fight), missile (a rocket), siren (a device which makes a loud warning noise). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US and Israel hit three places in Iran: Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan. Iran makes nuclear things in these places. The US drops big bombs from airplanes. The leaders say this is a strong attack, and it can bring peace . Iran sends many rockets back to Israel. The defense stops most of them. Sixteen people are hurt. One warning sound does not work in a town. An expert says that the attack is not right by international rules. He says Iran may work on its nuclear program secretly . He says talking is better than war. Difficult words: peace (the time without a war or fight), defense (technologies and people which keep a country safe), secretly (when you do something and others do not know about it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

European leaders responded to the US airstrikes on Iran with calls for diplomacy and restraint . Most supported preventing Iran from getting nuclear weapons but were not fully supportive of the strikes. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen asked Iran to return to talks, saying diplomacy is the only way to bring peace. Leaders of Estonia and Portugal also warned about further violence and stressed the need for respect for international law. Germany and the UK asked for calm responses and offered no clear support for the US action. Finland’s president warned against a cycle of revenge and said real peace must come from negotiations. Italy held a video meeting with top officials and said it would keep working to bring all parties to talks. France kept a more distant tone. Its foreign minister said France was not part of the strike plan and pushed for solutions under the nuclear treaty. President Macron called several Middle East leaders and urged Iran to show restraint. Difficult words: restraint (control of actions or emotions), revenge (hurting someone in return for what they have done to someone else). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

European leaders want Iran and others to return to peace talks . They say Iran should not make nuclear weapons. They don’t fully support the US attack but ask for calm and respect for international rules. Von der Leyen and other leaders said only talks can stop the danger. Finland and Germany say the violence must stop. Italy had a big meeting and said they would try to help the two sides talk. France didn’t support the US strikes and asked Iran to stay calm. Macron spoke with leaders in the Middle East and asked Iran to stop and talk again. Many leaders agree that only peace talks can bring safety. But Iran doesn’t seem ready to talk yet. Difficult words: peace talks (talks between countries or governments to end conflict), strike (an attack). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many leaders in Europe want peace talks with Iran. They say that Iran must not get a nuclear bomb. They do not say the US attack is good. But they want to stop fighting. Some leaders, like Ursula von der Leyen, want to talk more. Italy has a big online meeting with other leaders. They want to help the sides talk together. Finland says that fighting must stop. France does not join the US attack. Macron talks to leaders in the Middle East. He tells Iran to stay calm and talk. But Iran does not want to talk now. Difficult words: peace talks (talks between countries or leaders to stop a fight), side (one of the people or groups who take part in a fight, war, and so on), join (to take part). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Chinese city of Xuchang, located in Henan province, is a global leader in the wig industry, producing about 60 percent of the world’s wigs. There are over 4,100 companies and 300,000 workers in the area, with most wigs made from human hair. Originally, people in rural villages sold their hair to buyers. Today, wigs are still connected to fashion and beauty, although some people wear them for health reasons. Rebecca Hair Products, a major company in Xuchang, used to sell only to the United States. However, it later expanded its business to Africa, where wigs are part of daily life for many people. Now, wigs are popular in Africa, Europe, and other parts of the world. In 2024, the city exported more than 2 billion dollars in hair products. One shop owner in Nairobi, Kenya, says she first felt unsure about buying from China. But now she is very happy with the quality of the wigs and says no one in Kenya can copy them. Difficult words: wig (hair you wear on your head), rural (places that are in the countryside, not in cities or towns), expand (to grow or enter new areas). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Xuchang is a city in China. It makes more than half of the world’s wigs . There are many companies in the city, and a lot of people work there. Most wigs use real human hair. People in the countryside sell their hair to these companies. One big company is called Rebecca Hair. It first sold wigs only to the United States, but later, it started selling to Africa. In some African countries, wigs are part of everyday life. Wigs from Xuchang are now sold in many places around the world. In 2024, the city sold more than 2 billion dollars of hair products. A shop owner in Nairobi, Kenya, says she was nervous to buy from China at first. Now she is happy because the wigs are special and look very nice. Difficult words: wig (hair you wear on your head), countryside (places that are not cities), nervous (afraid or unsure). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Xuchang is a city in China. It makes many wigs . A wig is a hair you wear. Xuchang makes more than half of all wigs in the world. Many people work in wig shops. One big company is Rebecca Hair. It sells wigs to many countries. It sells wigs to Africa, the US, and Europe. Wigs are important in Africa. People wear them every day. A woman in Kenya has a wig shop. She buys wigs from China. At first, she feels scared . But now she feels happy. She likes the wigs. They are good and beautiful. No one in Kenya can make the same wigs. Difficult words: wig (hair you wear on your head), scared (worried, afraid). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Three-year-old Claire Bell remains missing following a disturbing series of events that have led to criminal charges against her mother, 34-year-old Rachel-Ella Todd. Todd appeared in court via video conference and was charged with child abandonment likely to cause permanent harm. Authorities in Quebec, Canada, launched an extensive search across the region, deploying helicopters, drones, and ground teams along highways 20 and 30, where the body of Claire’s dog was found. Public concern intensified after a TikTok video emerged showing Todd holding Claire and warning, “You try that again, and this is going to get ugly,” captioned with, “Have you ever faced a mother with nothing left to lose?” Police say Todd also made online searches related to children’s funeral urns . Though she has no prior criminal record, the Crown has opposed her release, and no psychiatric evaluation has yet been requested. Further charges may be added as the investigation continues and the search remains active. Difficult words: disturbing (worrying), intensify (to become stronger or more serious), funeral urn (a container holding the ashes of a cremated body). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Three-year-old Claire Bell from Quebec, Canada, went missing on Father’s Day. Her mother, Rachel-Ella Todd, age 34, is now in jail. Rachel went to court by video. Police are searching for Claire using helicopters, drones, and officers. They found Claire’s dead dog on the side of a road. Just hours before Claire disappeared, Rachel posted a video on TikTok. In it, she holds Claire and says, “You try that again, and this is going to get ugly .” Police say she also searched online for children’s funeral urns . Rachel had no problems with the police in the past and no mental health problems. The judge may add more charges . The next court date is Wednesday. Difficult words: ugly (bad, serious), funeral urn (a container to keep the ashes after a body is burned), charge (formally saying that you did something wrong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Claire Bell is a little girl. She is 3 years old. She lives in Quebec, Canada. She goes missing on Father’s Day. Her mother, Rachel-Ella Todd, is in jail. She is charged with leaving Claire alone. Rachel goes to court. The police are looking for Claire. They are using helicopters and many people. Claire’s little dog lies dead near a big road. Before Claire goes missing, Rachel posts a video on TikTok. She is holding Claire and saying scary words. Rachel also looks for funeral things online. Rachel will go to court again. The police are still looking for Claire. Difficult words: charge (to formally say that you do something wrong), scary (frightening), funeral (a ceremony when someone dies). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A major fire broke out at the New World Victoria Park supermarket in Auckland, New Zealand, and took 10 hours to extinguish. Firefighters remained at the site to monitor and control hot spots. The store was undergoing renovation, including recladding , modernization, and the addition of a new area for online order storage and distribution. Experts believe the fire started at the mezzanine level, where this work was taking place. The fire caused extensive damage, but the exact cause is still unknown. The next steps involve insurance assessors and engineers checking whether the building can be repaired or if it needs to be demolished and rebuilt. The building is complex, with a suspended floor and heavy truck-loading zones, which makes the engineering assessment more difficult. It may take years before a new supermarket opens on the site. Meanwhile, a large new supermarket is under construction in Christchurch. It will serve around 35,000 people a week. It has a large water tank for firefighting in case of emergencies. Difficult words: reclad (to put a new outside layer on a building), mezzanine (a small floor between two main floors in a building), assessor (a person who checks damage or cost). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A big fire happened at the New World supermarket in Auckland, New Zealand. Fire crews worked for 10 hours to stop the fire. The supermarket was getting repairs and a new area for online orders. The fire likely started in the upper part of the store, where builders were working. The reason for the fire is still not clear. The building is badly damaged. Now, insurance experts and engineers will look at it. They will check if the building can be fixed or if they need to take it down. Building a new one may take years. A big new supermarket is almost ready in Christchurch. Many people will shop there. It has a huge water tank to help in case of a fire. Difficult words: likely (probably), insurance (an agreement in which you pay a company money and they pay your costs if you have an accident, injury, and so on), huge (very big or large). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a big fire at the New World store in Auckland, New Zealand. Firefighters work many hours. They stop the fire. People build new things in the store. There is a new place for online shopping. The fire starts in the top part of the store. We do not know the reason. The building has a lot of damage . Some people are looking at the store now. They must say if it is possible to fix the building or make a new one. In another place, in Christchurch, a new big store is coming. It has a big water tank for fire. Difficult words: firefighter (a person who stops fires), damage (bad change to something), tank (a big container for water or other liquid). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Several recent influencer murders across India have shocked the country. In the case of Raja Raghuvanshi from Indore, new twists continue to emerge. Police are investigating missing phones and possible new people involved, including someone his wife, Sonam, reportedly contacted over 200 times. Investigators are exploring a suspected love triangle and have recreated the crime scene with the accused. A second murder weapon was found, and raids are ongoing in Indore. Sonam was in hiding for weeks before her arrest. In Haryana, former model and influencer Sheetal Chaudhary, known as Simmi, was murdered by her ex-boyfriend Sunil, who confessed but must do so before a magistrate for it to be valid in court. He had been harassing her, and she had called her sister in distress before she was killed. In Punjab, another influencer’s decomposed body was found in a car. Police say she was strangled. A religious vigilante , Amritpal Mehron, is the key suspect and fled India after recording a video justifying the act. These cases highlight a disturbing rise in violence by those closest to the victims. Difficult words: raid (a surprise attack by a small force), distress (extreme anxiety or pain), vigilante (a person who takes the law into their own hands). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In India, three influencers died recently. These crimes shocked many people. In Indore, someone killed Raja Raghuvanshi. Police are checking missing phones and say his wife Sonam, who is involved, talked a lot with another person. A love triangle may be part of the case. Police also found another phone. Police went to the crime scene with the people they arrested. In Haryana, model and influencer Sheetal Chaudhary was killed by her ex-boyfriend Sunil. He said he did it, but the court needs proof. Before she died, she told her sister Sunil was bothering her. In Punjab, another woman was found dead in a car. She was strangled . A man named Amritpal Mehron made a video and said he would kill people who hurt Punjab’s values. Police say he left India after the murder. These cases are scary because the killers were close to the people they killed. Difficult words: love triangle (a relationship in which three people are each in love with at least one other person), bother (to make someone feel worried or upset), strangle (to kill someone by pressing their throat). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Three influencers from India are dead. The police are looking at these sad cases . In Indore, a woman named Sonam is in trouble. The police find two weapons . They are checking her phone and the people she talks to. She is the wife of Raja Ranghuvanshi. He is dead. In Haryana, someone kills a woman named Sheetal Chaudhary. Her old boyfriend, Sunil, does it. Sheetal calls her sister before she dies. She is scared of Sunil. In Punjab, another woman dies. Her body is in a car. A man named Amritpal Mehron says bad things and makes a video. He says that he wants to kill people. Then he leaves India. In all these cases, the killers are close to the dead people. Difficult words: case (a situation that the police are working on), weapon (something what we use to hurt people), scared (afraid or not safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Schengen Agreement allows people and goods to move freely across many European countries without border checks. It has been in place for 40 years and is a key part of the European Union. However, countries like Germany and France have recently started to bring back border controls. They say this is because of irregular migration, pressure on asylum systems, and concerns about security and terrorism. Experts say these controls may be legal under Schengen rules, but they must only be temporary and for specific reasons. Some experts argue that countries are using border controls for political purposes, not because of real threats. These actions may go against the values of unity and cooperation that the EU supports. A law professor explains that while many parts of Schengen still work well, the visible problem is the return of internal border checks. This raises questions about how well Schengen can function if countries no longer fully respect the agreement. Difficult words: asylum (the protection a country gives to people who are escaping danger), temporary (lasting only for a short time), value (the important idea or principle). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Schengen Agreement started 40 years ago. It helps people and goods move between many European countries without border checks . But now, some countries like Germany are using border checks again. They want to control migration and stop problems with safety. Some experts say countries can use these checks only for a short time and only when there is a good reason. But many countries keep using them for a long time. Some people think these checks are more about politics than real danger. One professor says many parts of Schengen still work. But when countries start border checks again, it is a problem. People worry that this shows the European Union is not as strong and united as before. Difficult words: goods (things to buy and sell), border check (when officials or police stop people on the border of a country), united (working together as one group). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Schengen Agreement is 40 years old. It helps people and goods go between countries in Europe. They do not stop at borders . Now, some countries use border checks again. Germany is one of these countries. It wants to stop problems with people coming in. Some people say the checks are OK only for a short time. But some countries use them for a long time. This creates problems. Many people do not like the checks. One professor says that many things in Schengen work. But the checks at the borders are not good. They make travel slow. People want easy travel in Europe. They do not want new stops at borders. Difficult words: goods (things to buy and sell), border (the line between two countries), border check (when officials or police stop people on the border of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The UK and France have decided to show the British drama Adolescence in schools to raise awareness about violence, toxic masculinity , and the impact of social media on young people. The series follows a 13-year-old boy accused of killing a classmate and explores how male anger and online influencers like Andrew Tate affect teenagers. The show has received high praise for its strong performances and realistic storytelling. Critics call it a powerful tool to open discussions in classrooms. The decision comes after a rise in knife crimes and violent acts among students in both countries. The French and UK governments see the show as a chance to engage students with real issues and help them reflect on their own experiences. While most reactions have been positive, some UK politicians, like Boris Johnson, criticized the move, calling it political and unnecessary. However, the creators argue the show is about understanding modern masculinity, not race. Other countries may soon follow this cultural and educational approach. Difficult words: awareness (knowing that something exists), masculinity (qualities or behaviors thought to be typical of men), reflect (to think deeply or carefully about something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The UK and France want students to watch a British TV show called Adolescence. It is about a 13-year-old boy who is arrested after a classmate dies. The show talks about problems like anger in boys, knife crime, and bad things on social media. Many people like the show and say it is very real and emotional . Some teachers and parents think it can help students understand these problems. Both countries are worried about violence in schools. They also worry that social media is making teenagers think in a bad way. By showing this TV show, they want students to talk about these problems. Some people in the UK don’t agree. They think it is not good to show the drama in schools. The creators say the show is not about race but about problems boys face today. Difficult words: emotional (about a person’s feelings), violence (hurting someone), creator (a person who makes something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The UK and France show a TV show in schools. It is called Adolescence. It is about a boy. He is 13 years old. He is in trouble because girl in school dies. People want to talk about this show. Many people like the show. It talks about big problems. It shows how boys feel. It shows why some boys are angry. It shows bad things on social media . It helps students think about problems. Schools hope that the show will help students. They want to stop violence . Some people do not like the idea. But the people who made the show say it helps. Difficult words: trouble (a big problem), social media (webs and apps where people meet), violence (hurting other people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
